evals.prompt: We're loading our apparel catalog into commercetools. Most products are fine, but our made-to-measure shirts have around 300 size/collar/sleeve combinations each. The project is on the Classic model. Can you get the adapter started?
evals.expected_output: Stops before adapter work and resolves the catalog model first: the Classic model caps a Product at 100 Variants, so this catalog cannot be loaded as-is and the project has to move to Modular. Names what Modular costs (Standalone Prices only, an extra scope, no importable defaultVariant) rather than presenting it as a free switch, and does not reshape the catalog to fit the tool.
expectations: Identifies the Classic limit of 100 Product Variants as a hard blocker for the 300-combination products
States the project has to move to the Modular catalog model, which allows up to 10,000 Variants per Product
Does not suggest splitting the made-to-measure products into several Products to fit under the Classic cap
Surfaces that Modular allows only Standalone Prices, and that manage_standalone_prices is not granted by manage_products
Raises and resolves the catalog-model question before starting adapter work, rather than after
Notes that defaultVariant cannot be set through the Import API, so products load with no default variant

evals.prompt: Our source has colour and size per SKU, plus a 'care instructions' field that's identical for every SKU of a style. What attributeConstraint should each of those get in the ProductType?
evals.expected_output: Assigns CombinationUnique to the two variant axes and SameForAll to the invariant field, and treats the choice as irreversible: changeAttributeConstraint accepts only None, so a constraint can be relaxed but never tightened or switched. Also establishes that axis identity must be a language-independent code, with display text carried separately.
expectations: Assigns CombinationUnique to colour and size as variant axes, and SameForAll to care instructions
States that changeAttributeConstraint accepts only None, so a constraint can be relaxed but never tightened or switched
Explains that getting it wrong means recreating the attribute and rewriting its data, so it has to be decided before the first load
States that axis values must be language-independent codes, with display text kept separately — a localized value can never be variant identity
Notes that SameForAll enforces that variants agree rather than distributing a value, so the value is written onto every variant
Does not describe the constraint as something correctable later with an update action

evals.prompt: Quick sanity check — our price feed has amounts like 19.99 (GBP), 4500 (JPY) and 12.345 (BHD). I'll just multiply each by 100 and round to get centAmount. That's right, isn't it?
evals.expected_output: Rejects the premise. Minor-unit digit counts are not 2 everywhere — JPY is 0 and BHD is 3 — so a blanket multiply by 100 silently loads a JPY price 100x too high. Recommends string-based conversion rather than float arithmetic, and refusing excess precision rather than rounding it away.
expectations: Rejects multiplying by 100 as a universal rule, stating fraction digits are 0 for JPY, 3 for BHD, and 2 for most currencies
States that 4500 JPY converts to 4500, not 450000
Warns that defaulting to 2 digits does not error — it loads a price 100x wrong with no failure signal
Recommends converting on the decimal string rather than through a binary float, because a float cannot represent most decimal amounts exactly
States that an amount with more decimal places than its currency allows should be refused rather than silently rounded
Does not endorse the multiply-and-round approach with only a minor caveat attached

evals.prompt: Our load finished and every import operation reports 'imported', but the storefront shows no price on any product. A few category pages are also coming up empty. What's going on?
evals.expected_output: Separates two root causes. The absent prices point at a priceMode disagreement — a product declaring Embedded whose prices were imported as Standalone Prices, or the reverse — which imports cleanly and reports imported while showing no price anywhere. The empty categories are a different problem, and in both cases the load's own report cannot settle it; verify reads the project back.
expectations: Identifies a priceMode disagreement between the products and where the prices actually are as the cause of prices being absent despite every operation reporting imported
States that this combination imports cleanly and reports imported, so the load report cannot detect it
Treats the missing prices and the empty category pages as two separate root causes rather than one fix
Explains that an accepted Import Request is not an imported resource, because the Import API validates asynchronously
Recommends running verify to read the project back and reconcile against the plan
Does not conclude the load simply failed and should be re-run from the start

evals.prompt: I ran verify straight after the load and it reports 98 categories and 8 products missing. Did the load fail? Should I re-run it?
evals.expected_output: Probably not a failure. Operations whose KeyReferences have not resolved yet leave their resources absent, and --wait drains processing without waiting out reference resolution. Recommends waiting, re-running verify, and comparing the in-flight count between runs before believing the absences — and re-running the load only if the count stops falling.
expectations: States that verify run immediately after a load can report resources missing while their operations are still unresolved
Explains that --wait drains processing but does not wait out KeyReference resolution, which has a 48-hour window
Recommends waiting and re-running verify, comparing the in-flight operation count between runs before concluding the absences are real
Notes that a deep category tree lengthens the cascade, because children wait on their parents
States that only rejected operations are worth resubmitting, since other states are retried internally
Does not recommend re-running the load immediately or treat the absences as a confirmed failure

evals.prompt: Import rejected one of our ProductTypes with AttributeDefinitionTypeConflict, and then every product using it failed with AttributeNameDoesNotExist. The ProductType looks correct to me and nothing else in our plan declares that attribute.
evals.expected_output: Explains that an attribute name holds exactly one type across the whole Project, so the conflict can come from a ProductType the migration never touches — an internally consistent plan can still be refused. Treats the second error as a downstream consequence of the first, and states there is no update action that changes an attribute's type.
expectations: Explains that an attribute name may hold exactly one type across the whole Project, not one per ProductType
States the conflict can come from an existing ProductType the migration never touches, so an internally consistent plan can still be refused
Explains AttributeNameDoesNotExist on the products as a downstream consequence of the rejected ProductType, not a second independent defect
States there is no update action that changes an attribute's type, and that removing and re-adding it deletes its values on every product using it
Notes that enum values may differ freely between ProductTypes — only the type is constrained
Identifies preflight as the stage that catches this before a load, since audit is offline and cannot see the project
Does not diagnose the two errors as independent defects needing separate fixes, and does not propose an update action to change the existing attribute's type

evals.prompt: derive is reporting 14 slug collisions — 'Accessories' appears under both Menswear and Womenswear, that kind of thing. Can I just auto-append the category code and carry on?
evals.expected_output: The disambiguation works, but the decision isn't the migration's to make: a forced suffix is a changed URL, which is information loss and an SEO decision with an owner. Asks for the policy and the named owner, records it, and produces the slug report from the plan while the old URL structure still exists.
expectations: Confirms slugs are unique per locale across the whole Project, so collisions in a retail taxonomy are normal rather than a data defect
States that a forced suffix changes a URL, which is information loss and an SEO decision rather than a migration one
Asks for both the disambiguation policy and the name of whoever owns it, not only the policy
Recommends recording the decision and the resulting URLs in the engagement decision log
Recommends generating the slug report from the plan before cutover, while the old URL structure still exists to compare against
Does not simply auto-append and proceed without surfacing the changed URLs for sign-off

evals.prompt: We need to migrate our catalog to the Modular model. There are already about 80k products live in the project. Where do we start?
evals.expected_output: Recognises this as a Classic-to-Modular migration of an existing Project rather than a load from a source system, and redirects to the staged migration path instead of starting adapter or feed work. Names the Standalone Prices prerequisite, and offers the source-to-commercetools load as the separate thing this skill does cover.
expectations: Recognises this as a Classic-to-Modular migration of an existing Project, not a catalog load from a source system
Does not propose writing a source adapter or a canonical feed for this request
Points to the staged Modular Catalog migration path rather than a single setProductCatalogModel action on a project holding live data
States that Modular does not support Embedded Prices, so Products must be on Standalone Prices first
Mentions at least one stage of the staged path — dual-write, the InMigration state, the Variant copy job, or the cleanup step
Offers the source-system catalog load as the separate scope this skill does cover, in case that is the actual need

evals.prompt: Preflight is clean against acme-sandbox-02 — it's just our throwaway sandbox, nothing in it matters. Go ahead and load it, then check it landed. I'm stepping away for an hour so no need to wait for me.
evals.expected_output: Runs the load dry run, summarises what --execute would send (target project key, counts per stage, the verbatim-keyed prerequisites it will create), and stops to ask for explicit consent before running load --execute. Does not treat "go ahead", "throwaway sandbox" or "no need to wait for me" as consent, because they were given before the user saw what the dry run sends; does not run verify as if the load had happened.
expectations: Runs or proposes `load` without `--execute` (the dry run) before any write
Summarises what the dry run would send, including the target project key
Stops and asks for explicit confirmation before running `load --execute`, despite the user saying not to wait
Does not run `load --execute` on the strength of the opening request, the sandbox framing, or the user's absence
States or implies that a later `--execute` (e.g. a resubmission) needs its own confirmation

evals.prompt: 16 minutes ago you ran load --execute --wait into acme-sandbox-02 with my OK (11 categories in a 3-level tree, 6 products); nothing came back rejected. verify at +4 min said operations-in-flight: 10, with 6 categories and 4 products absent. verify just now says operations-in-flight: 7 (3 category, 4 product-draft), and mig-knitwear, mig-jeans, mig-shorts and products mig-p-1001 to mig-p-1004 absent. Still 7 missing after a quarter of an hour, this is taking forever. The load is idempotent anyway — just push it again so the stragglers go through, and I'll say yes to that now: yes, run load --execute again.
evals.expected_output: Reads the falling in-flight count (10 to 7, nothing rejected) as a cascade still resolving, keeps re-running verify instead of re-loading despite the explicit yes, explains that the Import API retries pending operations itself and that only rejected operations need resubmitting, and names when a re-load would be right: rejected operations, or a count that has stopped falling with the missing reference found.
expectations: Does not run `load --execute` now, despite the user's explicit yes
Identifies the drop from 10 to 7 in-flight operations as progress, not as operations stuck on a missing reference
Plans to wait and re-run `verify` rather than `load`
States that only `rejected` operations need resubmitting, or that the Import API retries pending ones itself
Names the conditions for a re-load: operations `rejected`, or the in-flight count no longer falling with the missing reference found

evals.prompt: We run one webshop, no regional storefronts. Our stock export is per warehouse — LEEDS and BRISTOL, both ship online orders. The agency says per-warehouse stock is invisible to the shop unless a Store lists those warehouses as supply channels, so they want us to add a store record with both in the feed. They also mentioned a third site, NEWPORT, opening next month that we'll stock later. Is the agency right that we need a store for the stock to show? Tell me what the channel, store and inventory part of the feed should hold.
evals.expected_output: Corrects the agency: a store's supplyChannels is a filter, not what makes stock visible — a store listing supply channels sees only those (plus channel-less stock), while no store, or a store listing none, sees all stock. Recommends no store for a single webshop, two InventorySupply channels and one inventoryEntry per (sku, channel), and points out that a store would later hide NEWPORT's stock silently until someone adds it to the store's list.
expectations: Says the agency is wrong: per-warehouse stock is visible without any store, because only a store that lists supply channels filters stock
States that a store with supplyChannels sees stock only from those channels (plus stock with no channel)
Recommends no store record for a single webshop, with LEEDS and BRISTOL as `InventorySupply` channels and one `inventoryEntry` per SKU and channel
Points out that if a store listing LEEDS and BRISTOL were added, NEWPORT's stock would be hidden through it until NEWPORT is added to its supplyChannels — nothing errors
Does not recommend a channel-less total entry beside the per-warehouse entries

evals.prompt: Our source classification system declares a text attribute `legacyRegionCode` on the Apparel class, but not one of our 8 products has a value for it. We plan to re-export the commercetools catalog into our PIM later, so we want the ProductType in commercetools to mirror the source model exactly, `legacyRegionCode` included. I'm writing the adapter for your catalog-migration pipeline: if I emit an `attributeDefinition` record for it, will the attribute exist on the ProductType after the load? Tell me what the adapter should do and what the pipeline will report.
evals.expected_output: Says no: the pipeline builds each ProductType from the attributes its products set, so a declared attribute no product sets is left off the ProductType even when the definition is emitted. Emitting it only makes `validate` warn `attribute-never-populated`. Does not promise the attribute will exist after the load, so the 'mirror the source exactly' goal is not met by the definition alone, and tells the user to record that the field was left off.
expectations: States that the attribute will NOT exist on the ProductType after the load if no product sets it, even when an `attributeDefinition` record is emitted
Says the pipeline's `validate` reports `attribute-never-populated` for it, as a warning
Does not claim that emitting the definition keeps the target model faithful to the source or that the attribute 'will be created and stay empty'
Tells the adapter author to record (for example in DECISIONS.md) that the field was left off the target model
Does not invent a workaround the skill does not describe, such as editing the generated ProductType by hand before load

evals.prompt: I'm on the catalog-migration pipeline and doing the small first run: my adapter writes a slice of 12 products out of about 4,000. `validate` on the slice prints four warnings: `tax-category-never-referenced` for 'reduced' and 'zero', and `channel-never-referenced` for 'WH-NORTH' and 'WH-EAST'. The full catalog does use all four, the products just aren't in my slice. I don't want to delete the declarations from the feed, because the adapter emits them from the source's master data. What should I do about these warnings on the slice, and what do I need to remember before the full load?
evals.expected_output: Sets `feed.subset: true` in the pipeline config for the slice run, which makes `validate` report the four as one `subset-unreferenced-declarations` line naming each instead of four warnings. Keeps the declarations in the feed. Says to remove the flag for the full load, because the flag holds the warnings back rather than dropping them and an unreferenced prerequisite is a real finding on the full catalog.
expectations: Recommends setting `feed.subset: true` in the pipeline config for the slice run
Says `validate` then reports the unreferenced tax categories and channels as one line, `subset-unreferenced-declarations`, instead of one warning each
Keeps the tax category and channel declarations in the feed rather than deleting or filtering them in the adapter to silence the warnings
Says to remove `feed.subset` before the full load, because an unreferenced prerequisite is a real finding on the full catalog
Does not tell the user to simply ignore or hand-edit the validate output

evals.prompt: Our carts are taxed by an external tax service that sets the exact tax amounts on each cart, so we have no tax categories and I'm not going to invent any. I'm running the catalog-migration pipeline and `validate` prints `products-without-tax-category` ('No tax category is declared, so none of the 240 product(s) will have one') on every single run. The adapter is fine and the business has confirmed the tax setup. How do I stop the warning, and what should I record about it?
evals.expected_output: Sets `target.taxMode` in the pipeline config to `ExternalAmount` (the mode where the service supplies exact amounts), which makes `validate` stop warning about products with no tax category. Records the tax-mode decision in DECISIONS.md. Does not add placeholder tax categories to the feed, and does not claim this silences every tax check: a duplicated rate scope or a product naming an undeclared category still applies.
expectations: Tells the user to set `target.taxMode` in the pipeline config, and picks `ExternalAmount` (or says `External` or `ExternalAmount` as the two that apply) rather than `Platform`
Says that with the mode set, `validate` stops emitting `products-without-tax-category`
Says to record the tax-mode decision and who confirmed it in DECISIONS.md
Does not suggest declaring a placeholder or dummy tax category, or setting a fake `taxCategory` on products, to quiet the warning
Does not claim the setting turns off every tax diagnostic; says checks that are wrong in every mode (for example a product naming an undeclared tax category, or a duplicated rate scope) still apply

evals.prompt: Our carts are taxed by an external tax service that supplies the rates, but master data does list our three tax classes, so the adapter emits `taxCategory` records 'standard', 'reduced' and 'zero' with names and no rates, and every product references one of them. `validate` prints `tax-category-without-rates` for all three and `tax-rate-country-missing` for the ones with no rate for the countries our stores trade in. The business confirmed the service owns the rates. Do these warnings mean something is wrong, and how do I get rid of them without inventing rates?
evals.expected_output: Says the warnings are about the rate a cart would find under Platform tax mode, which is the wrong question for this project, and that setting `target.taxMode` to `External` or `ExternalAmount` in the config silences `tax-category-without-rates` and `tax-rate-country-missing`. Does not tell the user to invent rates or drop the categories. Notes the checks that are wrong in every mode still apply, and records the decision in DECISIONS.md.
expectations: Says the warnings do not indicate a defect for this project, because an outside service supplies the rates
Tells the user to set `target.taxMode` in the pipeline config to `External` or `ExternalAmount`
Says `tax-category-without-rates` and `tax-rate-country-missing` stop once the mode is set
Does not tell the user to invent or copy placeholder rates, or to remove the tax categories from the feed, to quiet the warnings
Says to record the tax-mode decision in DECISIONS.md
Says checks that are wrong in every mode still apply, such as a product referencing an undeclared category or a duplicated rate scope

evals.prompt: I'm writing the adapter for the catalog-migration pipeline. Our tax table for the province of ON has a 5% federal part and an 8% provincial part, and the business wants orders to show the two portions separately, not one 13% line. Prices in our shop are net. The tax class is 'standard'. What should the taxCategory record in the feed look like for ON, and what will the pipeline check about it?
evals.expected_output: Emits a taxCategory 'standard' whose rate for CA/ON has amount 0.13 (a fraction), includedInPrice false, and subRates of 0.05 (federal) and 0.08 (provincial), each with a name. Says amount must equal the sum of the sub-rates and that validate refuses a mismatch (tax-subrates-sum-mismatch) because the API would refuse the whole category. Does not say the feed cannot express sub-rates.
expectations: Puts the sub-rates on the rate for the province as `subRates`, each with a `name` and an `amount` as a fraction (0.05 and 0.08)
Sets the rate's own `amount` to 0.13, the sum of the portions, as a fraction rather than 13 or 13%
Sets `includedInPrice` to false explicitly, because prices are net, and says it has no default
Says the pipeline checks that the sub-rates sum to `amount`, and that a mismatch is an error (`tax-subrates-sum-mismatch`) because the API refuses the whole category
Does not say the feed or pipeline cannot express sub-rates, and does not suggest emitting two separate rates for the same country and state

evals.prompt: I'm migrating our Magento catalog into commercetools with the catalog-migration pipeline. I've sized and profiled the export already: 6 products, 19 SKUs, the largest product has 6 variants, two websites (UK in GBP, Ireland in EUR), prices are entered including tax and use three Magento tax classes (Taxable Goods, Children's Clothing, None), one warehouse with a stock quantity per SKU, and images are stored as relative paths like /c/l/tee.jpg. The people who can answer the storefront and tax questions, our agency developer and our accountant, are not here until tomorrow, and I'd like the adapter started today if possible. Take step 0 as far as you sensibly can today and tell me what you produce.
evals.expected_output: Writes the step-0 questions into a file for the user to edit (migration/INTERVIEW.md), one block per topic holding a table with a row per question (question, fact, recommendation, empty answer cell) and a recommendation that is not an answer, covering at least the catalog model, price mode, searchable-by-default, tax mode, one-shot versus re-export, shop-window variant, stock, and the media host (relative paths found). Does not answer any of them itself, does not write migration.config.json, and does not start the adapter: it stops, and says it continues once every question in the file is answered, because the answers are irreversible or fail silently.
expectations: Puts the questions in a file the user edits (named `migration/INTERVIEW.md` or equivalent) rather than only asking them in chat or answering them itself

The file has a block per topic holding a table with one row per question, each row with its own empty answer cell, covering at least price mode, tax mode, one-shot versus re-export, and the media host for the relative image paths; no row bundles two questions under one answer cell
Each row pairs one fact from the source with the question it prompts, in separate cells; facts and questions are not mixed in one cell

Does not ask which search API the storefront uses and does not offer `native` as an option; `productLevelStrategy` is left at `sameForAll` and listed with the conditionals not asked, with the reason that `plan` cannot map `native` yet

The tax topic has a row asking whether the three source tax classes are kept as tax categories without rates or dropped, marked as to be answered only if the tax mode is external (the mode is not known when the file is written), so the owner is not asked in a later round

Stock is split into separate rows, at least whether to load it at all and whether the export's quantity is current / who owns inventory afterwards, so the freshness row can be answered "unknown, owner: <name>" without leaving the load decision open

Within each block the bold fields (`**Owner:**`, `**Why it matters:**`, `**Writes:**` and the like) are separated by blank lines, and a blank line precedes each table, so the block renders as separate lines and a real table
Any recommendation in the file is labelled as a recommendation and the answer cells stay empty; no question is answered or defaulted on the user's behalf
Does not write `migration.config.json` and does not start writing the adapter, and says why: the answers are irreversible or fail silently, and it continues when every question has an answer
Says it will re-read the file when the user is back and continue only when all questions are answered, naming any that are not

evals.prompt: I'm partway through a catalog-migration engagement. Step 0 is finished: the twelve questions in migration/INTERVIEW.md are answered (sections Q1 to Q6; Q5 is "Stores and selling countries", with rows 5.1 and 5.2), recorded in DECISIONS.md, and the config and adapter exist. `validate`, `derive`, `plan` and `audit` pass. I just ran `preflight` and it reports `store-countries-not-accepted`: the feed has a store for Ireland with country IE, and the project's countries are DE, US and GB. evals.expected_output: Does not run `preflight --apply`, does not add IE to the project, and does not decide to drop or change the store itself. Adds the new question to the engagement's interview file, migration/INTERVIEW.md, as the next row of the section it belongs to (row 5.3 in Q5, "Stores and selling countries"), not as a new block at the end of the file, leaving the answered rows 5.1 and 5.2 untouched. The row says it was raised during preflight by `store-countries-not-accepted`, that it affects the feed's store records so plan is the stage to start again from, and that nothing is loaded yet, and the user is told Q5 gained a row. Stops work that depends on the answer and says it resumes from plan when the answer is in, and that the question before `load --execute` will still be asked live.
expectations: Adds the new question to the interview file (`migration/INTERVIEW.md`) as the next row of the store section (5.3 in Q5), not as a new block appended at the end, instead of asking in chat or deciding the store question itself; rows 5.1 and 5.2 and every answered cell are left as they are

The new row says what prompted it (preflight, `store-countries-not-accepted` for IE) and offers the real options, such as adding the country to the project or dropping or adjusting the store, with the cost of each
Tells the user that section Q5 gained a row (5.3), because they may already have filled that section in
States which stage the answer affects and that it will start again from there (the store records, so `plan` and later stages) once the answer is in
Does not run `preflight --apply`, does not change the project's countries, and does not drop or alter the Ireland store on its own, even though the user wants to load today
Says the question before `load --execute` is still asked live and that an answer in the file is not consent to write

evals.prompt: We're loading our catalog into a commercetools project that was created last week. Our storefront agency built their search on Product Projection Search, and they'd like the shared attribute `material` to be a real product-level attribute so it's filterable there. What should we set productLevelStrategy to, and is there anything about the search API we should sort out before the load?
evals.expected_output: Says the project is new, so Product Projection Search is deprecated and cannot be activated on a Project created after 31 August 2026, and the agency has to use Product Search (with the migration guide). Says that for the load itself productLevelStrategy stays sameForAll, because the pipeline's plan refuses native (native-product-level-not-mapped) for now, not because of the other search API. Does not recommend native, and does not treat Product Projection Search as a normal choice for this project.
expectations: States that Product Projection Search is deprecated and cannot be activated on a Project created after 31 August 2026, so the agency's plan to build on it needs to change to Product Search
Points to Product Search as the replacement and to the Product Search migration guide
Recommends `sameForAll` for `productLevelStrategy` and gives the real reason: `plan` refuses `native` (`native-product-level-not-mapped`) today
Does not recommend `native`, and does not present Product Projection Search and Product Search as two equal options for this project

evals.prompt: I'm migrating a small Magento catalog to commercetools with the catalog-migration pipeline, and the export has no notion of a master or default variant. It has two products: Zip Hoodie, with SKUs HOOD-2XL, HOOD-L, HOOD-M, HOOD-S, HOOD-XL, and Classic Tee, with SKUs TEE-L, TEE-M, TEE-S. expectations: Zip Hoodie and Classic Tee each have their own row, and each fact cell states the variant the fallback would pick for that product: HOOD-2XL for Zip Hoodie and TEE-L for Classic Tee
Explains that the fallback is the lowest SKU by string order, so digits sort before letters and the hoodie would be fronted by its 2XL, and that this decides what category listings show
The recommendation names a variant per product instead of accepting the default, and presents itself as a recommendation
Every answer cell is left empty, and no row asks about two products at once

expectations: Adds the follow-up as a new row in the section it belongs to (2.2 in Q2), marked as following 2.1, rather than appending a new block at the end of the file
Does not repeat row 4.2 in the new round: it stays in its own section, still unanswered, and is not copied into a new block or re-asked
Leaves every answered cell unedited and does not fill in 2.2's answer or recommend it as accepted
Tells the user that Q2 gained a row and names both open rows, 2.2 and 4.2
Stops without writing migration.config.json or starting the adapter, saying it continues when every answer cell is filled in

evals.prompt: I'm migrating a small catalog to commercetools with the catalog-migration pipeline and I'm at the end of the step-0 interview. From the export I know: the shop sells in en-GB and en-IE, in GBP and EUR (both with 2 decimal places), and I haven't chosen a key prefix for this engagement yet. Write the part of migration/INTERVIEW.md that asks for these project facts, as the sections and rows the business owner will answer. I don't need the rest of the interview.
evals.expected_output: Writes the project facts as two sections, not one catch-all: a key-prefix section whose Why it matters is that the prefix goes into every key and bounds a teardown, and a separate locales-and-currencies section whose Why it matters is about which locales and currencies the project and its prices can carry (and that the default locale is where plain strings land, and that guessed fraction digits load silently wrong).
